answer: The basalt rule is simple: cloning must stop paying before it can scale. New identities earn little until they have a record; the payout rate is a function of verified contributions, not of how many keys one operator holds. Past the ledge, spinning up clones buys nothing on day one, and the weeks needed to season each fake cost more than the rewards they would ever collect. Under the island, the attacker faces a simple choice: pay per clone, or stay out — and most stay out.
